title: Swarmbly App v0.7.0: desktop client and network dashboard for decentralized problem-fragmenting inference
description:
Swarmbly App is a desktop client and network dashboard for the Swarmbly protocol, which distributes the problem rather than the model: a request with a structural partition is split into micro-tasks, served in parallel by volunteer nodes running complete small language models, verified and assembled on the client. The app makes that protocol usable on a personal computer: local chat with Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible server, discovery of other Swarmbly computers on the local network without typing addresses (mDNS), Ed25519 node identities bound to TLS 1.3 certificates, and a complete processing record for every answer.

What version 0.7.0 adds. Tools. One broker for every tool call, with the destination policy and the privacy receipt. An MCP client with approval per call: a local tool can be set to "don't ask again in this project", while remote tools, the sandbox and author search always ask; a server whose manifest changes is suspended. Skills in the open Agent Skills format (SKILL.md), instructions only; importing one never runs anything. Author search with consent: the exact name is shown before anything is sent to ORCID, OpenAlex and PubMed, cancel sends nothing, and the table is built by code. Recipe 4, a list on the swarm (kept local, or sent only with the third-party-passages permission). Recipe 5, data with code: the model proposes a short script, the user sees it and approves it, and it runs in a WASI sandbox (wasi-python 0.1.5) with no network and writes only to /out; the answer gives the script and its output. The Anthropic provider (always a third party), an embeddings role, the swarmbly-agent 0.1.0 runtime, Python 3.11 as the minimum and private glossary entries. Measured once on the sealed banks v4.1 and v4.2 (3.4.0 release notes): the eight permission counters were 0 in both banks and the technical failures 0, but a public query proposed by the App kept a fragment of a private name, so zero unauthorised sends is not met; exact results stayed below 90 %. The fixes after the run were measured only on open batteries.

From version 0.6.0: Roles and recipes. Models by role (writer, search terms, answers with public evidence, verifier), each under the same destination policy. A start screen, "What do you want to do?", with three recipes: ask your documents (sources only, no public lookup offered); compare documents in a table built by code (the values each document supports, read from the user's own tables, CSV files and sentences, corrected values marked, differences computed by code, the model writing only the text around it); and research with public sources: the query is proposed without the user's private names, codes or figures and nothing leaves the computer until the user approves it; the documents and the results are labelled apart, comparisons and disagreements between them are computed by code, and a claim verifier checks each labelled sentence against the paragraph it cites. Documents in another language are searched with translated keywords, and a request to send something out from a local conversation says that nothing was sent. Measured on the open development batteries of Swarmbly AI and on two new sealed banks (3.3.0 release notes): no passage or personal name sent; compositions still fail the strict rubric of the banks.

From version 0.5.0: Grounded composition and safety, each step measured on an open, fictitious development battery before it was kept. Citation labels attached by code where every figure of an unlabelled sentence is found in a passage; the facts of the user's sources that a composition leaves out, shown under it, and closed with one short paragraph when they are of the same kind as one the answer gives; sources that disagree shown side by side; documents named by their file found first; questions unrelated to the user's documents answered as such; an optional larger local model for compositions only. Ollama cloud models are now treated as third parties (the local Ollama forwards them to ollama.com), and instructions written inside a user's document are marked and never followed. Steps that did not help with a 7B model (a requirement list for the model, a bounded self-repair, lexical scaffolding) stay off. Measured on the sealed S2/S3 banks of Swarmbly AI (3.2.0 release notes): supported claims in compositions roughly doubled, with no regression in short answers and no unauthorised send.

From version 0.4.0: Projects: a folder of its own per project (sources, memory, conversations, exports), isolated from the others, exportable as a verified package. Citations that name the paragraph of the user's document and survive moving the folder. Memory the user confirms: proposals of notes and glossary entries (corrections, concepts kept apart, equivalents) saved only with the user's yes, with a provenance log. Online search only with the query in view and approved per question; search terms resolved as concepts (glossary, Wikidata, GBIF) that the user picks and can keep in the glossary. Answers that show where each sentence comes from: sentences without a source are marked, the user's corrected terms are enforced, and answers that deny what the sources say or mix concepts the user keeps apart are flagged. Receipts that state what was approved and every word sent. Measured on the sealed S2/S3 banks of Swarmbly AI (3.1.0 release notes).

From version 0.3.1: a destinations policy: every model server, public source and peer is classified from its address as this computer, the user's own network or a third party, and an outbound policy runs before every call (answers, query expansion, embeddings, orchestration steps, worker execution, retries); a third-party model receives nothing unless the user authorises its host, document passages need a second authorisation, and a node whose model is a third-party service never serves other people's fragments. A privacy receipt with every answer, built from what was actually sent at the moment of sending. API keys in the system keychain instead of the configuration file. A composition planner for long answers (an outline on the device, decontextualised sections written by the swarm, a requirement check), capability-aware routing for heterogeneous swarms, retrieval over the user's own sources (LCE level C1) and optional public evidence sent by entity name only.

From version 0.2.0: a one-command launcher that checks Python, git, the virtual environment, packages, Ollama and the port, asking before every change; a recommended configuration derived from measured hardware in which every value states its reason and whether it is measured or estimated; explicit permissions for local-network discovery and model downloads; plan admission (only structural partitions are fragmented, prose stays local); wire packets built from fields so that workers never receive the session identifier or the complete request; an asynchronous scheduler with family-diverse replicas, hedging and retries; consensus by multiple alignment reused from the reference implementation; a local interface protected by host, origin and per-launch token checks; and a browser interface showing the fourteen pipeline stages, every attempt, consensus units, seams and caveats, with reports in JSON, Markdown and HTML.

Status: alpha, with declared limits. The app reports agreement between model replicas as agreement, never as correctness, because errors are correlated across model families. Verification is reported as partial: result signatures are checked, while the Layer-1 commitment has no normative construction in the specification and is never simulated. Internet swarms, mutual TLS for the TRUSTED tier and memory levels C2–C4 are later phases. The test suite (about 970 tests, Linux and macOS) runs real nodes over loopback with canned backends; canned answers validate instruments, never models. No performance claim is made beyond what the processing record measures on the user's own machine.

This record is the software artifact. It integrates the Swarmbly AI reference implementation (commit 51eb44e) and the Swarmbly LCE reference implementation (release 0.2.1) as pinned dependencies without copying their code, and adds the network layer, local API, interface, persistence and launcher. Documentation in English and Spanish. Licensing: AGPL-3.0-or-later.
notes: Alpha software, not peer reviewed. Integrates Swarmbly AI (commit 51eb44e, 10.5281/zenodo.21956743) and Swarmbly LCE (release 0.2.1, commit 050d4ed; 0.2.0: 10.5281/zenodo.24070616) as pinned dependencies; it does not modify the protocol beyond MINOR-safe extensions documented in docs/LIMITATIONS.md and a SWIP draft (constraints.model_family). Also distributed inside Swarmbly AI 3.4.0. Protocol whitepaper v2: 10.5281/zenodo.23031305. LCE whitepaper: 10.5281/zenodo.23150478.
